To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have crystallized the major horse allergenic protein, Equ c 1, which belongs to the lipocain superfamily.

we have crystallized the recombinant form Equ c 1, a major horse allergen belonging to the lipocalins, that Equ c 1 exists in solution as a dimer and that we have collected data to 2. 9 A resolution using frozen crystals.
Equ c 1 crystallizes readily in a form suitable for X-ray diffraction analysis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular basis of allergenicity of Equ c 4 and the structure of its complex with IgE antibodies.
the structural characterization of Equ c 4 and Equ c 1, two major allergens of horse, and their interaction with IgE and T-cell receptor molecules, respectively.
the structure determination of Equ c 2, a major allergen from horse serum.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the structure of Equ c 2 is a dimer of two monomers with the same fold and similar binding sites as in other lipocalins.

the structure determination of Equ c 2 will allow us to understand the structural basis of the IgE cross-reactivity between horse allergens and to provide a structural basis for the design of specific immunotherapeutic agents for the treatment of equine hypersensitivity diseases.
the crystallization of the allergen Equ c1 is a successful example for the use of a frozen crystal for the collection of X-ray diffraction data at the synchron source.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Equ c 1 crystallizes in a space group which allows the formation of dimers in the crystal lattice.
we have successfully purified, crystallized and characterized the recombinant form and the native form of the horse allergen Equ C1.
Equ c 1 crystallizes readily in a form suitable for high-resolution structure determination, and that the protein exists as a dimer in solution.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Equ c 1 can be expressed and purified as a soluble, stable protein in Escherichia coli, and that the recombinant form is a suitable target for structural analysis.
the crystallization conditions used here can be applied for other lipocalins and may be useful for other members of the allergen superfamily.
the glycosylation pattern is different for the native Equ c 1 and the recombinant Equ c 1, which might explain why the recombinant protein has a higher IgE-binding activity than the native protein.
